description: The earliest reliable accounts of coffee drinking come from Yemen and Sufi monks in Yemen are reported to have used coffee to help them stay awake during nighttime prayers
Coffee had spread from Yemen to other parts of the Arabian Peninsula, including Mecca and Medina
Coffeehouses began appearing in cities across the region where people could drink coffee, talk, listen to music, and exchange news
Venetian merchants traded coffee with the Ottoman Empire, and coffee began to appear in Venice
First coffeehouses were established in England
Lloyd's Coffee House became a meeting place for merchants and people involved in maritime insurance
The Dutch established coffee cultivation in their colonies, including Java in the Dutch East Indies
location: Java in the Dutch East Indies

description: European colonial powers established coffee plantations in tropical regions of the Americas and the Caribbean
